newsitem.title: ITALY: GOLF-OLAZABAL, LANGER IN RYDER CUP POINTS CHASE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-OLAZABAL, LANGER IN RYDER CUP POINTS CHASE.

text.p: With five of the top six European Ryder Cup players featuring in the Italian Open which begins on Thursday, there could be a flurry of place-swapping by Sunday night.
But a great deal of interest will surround two men not in those lofty positions, Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal and Bernhard Langer of Germany.

Neither player has many more than a dozen tournaments left this year to qualify, Olazabal still insistent on playing two events and then resting his rehabilitating feet after the 18-month injury layoff and Langer committed elsewhere from the European Tour.
Both are mindful of the need to qualify automatically in a top-10 ranking by August 31 when the team is selected but will not up their schedules.
"I have to think about my feet so I won't be playing any more than two weeks at a time," said Olazabal, 15th in the Ryder rankings.

He is playing his second successive event after last week's Spanish Open 11th place, before his usual layoff, then appearing for two tournaments in Britain -- the English Open and PGA Championship -- before a rest and then his build-up to the U.S. Open.

Langer's seventh spot in the U.S. Masters largely helped him to 13th in the Cup table and he seeks a victory (something he did not achieve on the European Tour last year for the first time in 17 years) soon, so that his Ryder place will be almost a formality.
"I only have 10 or 11 events left before the team is chosen so it leaves me far more limited than most players on attaining automatic selection," said Langer.
"But I try to pick up good points every week and then I know just one win will get me into the team. Nobody can expect a wild card by right so that has to be the aim -- or a good few top-fives."

Both aim for a 78,330 points first prize. Ian Woosnam, currently going through putting problems which he claimed spoiled his U.S. Masters bid, is another who can benefit in the table by capturing the top prize, the Welshman lying eighth in the points table.

England's Jim Payne defends at Brescia, while home favourite Costantino Rocca (Ryder table 2nd), from just down the road at Bergamo, where Payne won last year, is also favourite to carry off victory. Miguel Martin (3rd in the table), Thomas Bjorn (4th), Paul Broadhurst (5th) and Darren Clarke (6th) are all in the battle for Cup points.
